_help: This file shows the format. Copy it, replace the examples with your own, and load it on the board's setup screen.
Choices: put the CORRECT answer first (answer: 0). The game shuffles the choices every time.
Every round's list is a bank. 'count' is how many are drawn each game. Add more than you need so games vary.
Rounds can be in any order. Keep one of each type: trivia, fib, draw, final. 'mult' multiplies that round's points.
title: Seminary Review Night
welcome: Join on your phone with the room code.
Answer on your phone, not out loud.
Points get bigger every round, and the finale lets you wager.

rounds.title: Quick Quiz
rounds.intro: Questions on what we've studied this year.
rules: A question and choices appear on the screen. Pick one on your phone.
The clock starts after the question is read aloud.
A correct answer scores. A faster correct answer scores a little more.
rounds._help: questions: q is the question. choices: the correct answer FIRST. answer: 0. note: shown after the reveal.

questions.q: EXAMPLE: Which book comes first in the Bible?
EXAMPLE: Which scripture says “Trust in the Lord with all thine heart”?

rounds.title: Fake Out
rounds.intro: Write a believable fake ending, then find the real one.
rules: Your set of 3 or 4 gets one clue. Write a fake ending that sounds real.
Everyone else sees the real ending mixed in with the fakes and picks the one they trust.
Pick the real one and score. Fool a classmate with your fake and score every time.
rounds._help: clues: prompt ends mid-sentence with ____. answer: the real ending. alt: other wordings that count as the real answer (students can't submit them as fakes). ref: shown after the reveal. house: 2 or more fakes used when students write too few.

clues.prompt: “Trust in the Lord with all thine heart; and ____”
clues.answer: lean not unto thine own understanding
alt: lean not to thine own understanding
house: call upon his name each morning
seek his counsel in all thy plans

clues.prompt: “In all thy ways acknowledge him, and ____”
house: he shall guide thee in peace
thou shalt find rest unto thy soul

rounds.title: Sketch It
rounds.intro: Draw a scripture story and guess your classmates' drawings.
rules: Your set draws the same story on your phone. No words or letters.
Everyone else sees the drawings and guesses which story it is.
Guess right and score. Draw clearly, because you score when classmates guess your story. Pick a favorite drawing for a bonus.
rounds._help: stories: story is what to draw (it must be drawable). ref: shown after the reveal. Keep count a bit above the number of sets (7 works for up to 20 students). Needs at least 2.

stories.story: EXAMPLE: A family choosing to serve the Lord together
EXAMPLE: Two sticks becoming one in a hand

rounds.title: The Final Question
rounds.intro: One hard question. Everything is on the line.
rules: Wager first, anywhere from nothing up to your whole score.
The choices are close, so read carefully.
Right: you win your wager. Wrong: you lose it. Audience members who answer correctly score too.
rounds._help: finals: one is drawn each game. Use 5 or 6 close choices, correct answer first, answer: 0.

finals.q: EXAMPLE: “…and call the sabbath a delight, the holy of the Lord, ____.”
